Saturday: A shift in the weather pattern is underway as the 
ridge of high pressure responsible for the mild temperatures 
and/or cool temperatures and persistent fog and stratus is 
shifting east and several Pacific waves cross into the Pacific 
Northwest. The first wave is coming through the region tonight 
and will slowly depart on Saturday to the east. Rainfall with 
this system will be light and snow levels will remain high 
enough such that only light, wet snow will impact Washington 
Pass Saturday morning. The front will bring a shift back to 
south to southwest winds with gusts in the afternoon of 15 to 20
mph. Temperatures will not cool back to mid November standards 
but areas that were experiencing the 60s on Friday will cool 
back into the 50s with 40-50s for most other lowlands.

The next system will arrive Sunday.  This will be another 
weakening cold front which will track through very slowly and 
allow a slow infiltration of cooler air. The next front will 
have a similar fetch of atmospheric moisture to work with but we
are expecting more rainfall than Saturday. This is largely due 
to the dry air currently in place becoming modified and 
moistened and once again, very slowly progression of the front 
from west to east. Many areas of North Idaho and eastern third 
of WA can expect between a tenth and quarter inch of rain with a
50-70% chance for receiving a quarter of an inch or more. Lower
amounts are expected in the lee of the Cascades and into the 
Western Basin where amounts will be less than a tenth of an 
inch. As for the passes, Washington Pass will carry the highest 
probabilities for several inches of snow with the forecast 
calling for 2-4 inches. Lookout and Stevens Passes will be 
transitioning from rain to snow or experience a mix at times 
through the event with lower probabilities for impacts. Light 
snow will also be possible over Sherman with around a 10% chance
for receiving an inch or more. Rain and areas of fog will be 
the main impacts to travel across the lowlands. 

Sunday's front will get hung up over far southeastern WA and 
the Idaho Panhandle Monday with additional periods of light 
rain. Additional light snow showers will impact the Cascade 
Crest. Much of Central and Eastern WA will be void of 
precipitation but will remain very moist with areas of low 
clouds and fog. The upper-level trough will slowly migrate 
through the region Monday night into Tuesday with the air mass 
continuing to slowly cool. 850mb temperatures will cool closer 
to 0 Celsius or within a degree. There is a slight risk for rain
to transition to wet snow on the higher benches of the Camas 
Prairie and Central Panhandle Mountains early Tuesday morning 
before the band of light precipitation finally shifts east. 
Otherwise, Tuesday and much of Wednesday have moderate 
probabilities to remain precipitation free as one system departs
and another deep low wobbles into Oregon. There remains 
considerable uncertainty with the track of this incoming system;
50% of the ensembles favoring a track south of the Inland NW 
through N CA and Oregon while 50% are further north across WA-
OR. With a cooler air mass in place, this will need to be 
monitored closely for more impactful snow on the mountain passes
and mix of rain and wet snow for some lowlands as we head into 
Thursday and Friday. At this time, confidence is low for 
accumulating lowland snow but seeing a few ingredients, which if
they align could tip the scale one way or another. Snow in the 
mountains seems more likely if the system takes a northern more 
track with potential for winter travel conditions from light 
accumulations. 

By the weekend: There is decent agreement that high pressure 
will return to the Northwest bringing another period of light 
winds and dry conditions. There is a strong likelihood that this
will promote another period of expansive fog and low clouds 
following in the wake of precipitation events this week. This 
will likely result in cooler, near normal temperatures given the
poor mixing and this is reflected in the latest NBM MaxT which 
comes with highs in the 30s to lower 40s. /sb
